title: The Free Radical Substitution Mechanism
page_title: The Free Radical Substitution Mechanism | Edexcel International A Level (IAL) Chemistry Revision Notes 2018

titles.section: 1. Structure, Bonding & Introduction to Organic Chemistry

blocks.md: - The free-radical substitution reaction consists of three steps:

- In the **initiation** **step,** the Cl-Cl or Br-Br is broken by energy from the UV light
- This produces two radicals in a **homolytic** **fission** reaction

blocks.alt: Hydrocarbons Initiation Step, downloadable AS & A Level Chemistry revision notes

blocks.md: ***The first step of the free-radical substitution reaction is the initiation step, in which two free radicals are formed by sunlight***

- The **propagation** **step** refers to the **progression **(growing) of the substitution reaction in a **chain reaction**

  - **Free radicals **are very reactive and will attack the unreactive alkanes
  - A C-H bond breaks **homolytically **(each atom gets an electron from the covalent bond)
  - An **alkyl** free radical is produced
  - This can attack another chlorine/bromine molecule to form the **halogenoalkane** and **regenerate** the chlorine/bromine free radical
  - This free radical can then **repeat **the cycle

blocks.alt: Hydrocarbons Propagation Step, downloadable AS & A Level Chemistry revision notes

blocks.md: ***The second step of the free-radical substitution reaction is the propagation step in which the reaction grows in a chain reaction***

- This reaction is not very suitable for preparing specific halogenoalkanes as a **mixture **of substitution products are formed

  - If there is enough chlorine/bromine present, all the hydrogens in the alkane will eventually get substituted (eg. ethane will become C<sub>2</sub>Cl<sub>6</sub>/C<sub>2</sub>Br<sub>6</sub>)

blocks.alt: Hydrocarbons Side-Products, downloadable AS & A Level Chemistry revision notes

blocks.md: ***The free-radical substitution reaction gives a variety of products and not a pure halogenoalkane***

- The **termination step **is when the chain reaction **terminates **(stops) due to two free radicals reacting together and forming a single unreactive molecule

  - Multiple products are possible

blocks.alt: Hydrocarbons Termination Step, downloadable AS & A Level Chemistry revision notes

blocks.md: ***The final step in the substitution reaction to form a single unreactive molecule***

blocks.text: Limitations of the free radical mechanism

blocks.md:
- In the termination step, there are a number of possibilities
- Remember that termination involves any free radical bonding with another free radical
- If we have two <sup>•</sup>CH<sub>3 </sub>radicals, they can bond to form ethane, CH<sub>3</sub>CH<sub>3</sub>

  - <sup>•</sup>CH<sub>3 </sub>+ <sup>•</sup>CH<sub>3</sub> → CH<sub>3</sub>CH<sub>3</sub>
  - If we are trying to form a chloroalkane, then ethane is an impurity

- Excess chlorine present when reacted with methane in the presence of UV light will promote further substitution and could produce CH<sub>2</sub>Cl<sub>2, </sub>CHCl<sub>3,</sub> CCl<sub>4</sub>
- Further substitution can occur as follows

  - CH<sub>3</sub>Cl + <sup>•</sup>Cl → HCl + <sup>•</sup>CH<sub>2</sub>Cl
  - <sup>•</sup>CH<sub>2</sub>Cl + Cl<sub>2</sub> → CH<sub>2</sub>Cl<sub>2 </sub>+ <sup>•</sup>Cl
- These reactions could occur

  - CH<sub>3</sub>Cl + Cl<sub>2</sub> → CH<sub>2</sub>Cl<sub>2 </sub>+ HCl
  - CH<sub>2</sub>Cl<sub>2</sub> + Cl<sub>2</sub> → CHCl<sub>3 </sub>+ HCl
  - CHCl<sub>3 </sub>+ Cl<sub>2</sub> → CCl<sub>4</sub> + HCl

- If we have an alkane with a middle carbon such as propane, substitution can occur here
- Propagation steps for the substitution of propane with excess bromine in the presence of UV light on the middle carbon are as follows:

  - CH<sub>3</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>CH<sub>3 </sub>+ <sup>•</sup>Br → CH<sub>3</sub><sup>•</sup>CHCH<sub>3 </sub>+ HBr
  - CH<sub>3</sub><sup>•</sup>CHCH<sub>3 </sub>+ Br<sub>2</sub> → CH<sub>3</sub>CH(Br)CH<sub>3</sub> + <sup>•</sup>Br
- If the question asks for the halogen to be substituted onto a middle carbon, you must show the radical dot in the correct place, so on the electron-deficient carbon
